title: About us
content: ### MULTIVAC - Packaging and processing solutions designed and built for your success. Packaging machines & packaging technology, automation solutions & processing technology, labelling and inspection systems, portioning and slicing - and, since the takeover of the FRITSCH Group, bakery technology as well. For more than 60 years, MULTIVAC has been one of the leading manufacturers of packaging machines. Company headquarters - as well as the nucleus of the now global MULTIVAC Group - are located in Wolfertschwenden, Germany. 16 production sites, state-of-the-art Application Centers, best-in-class service and support, comprehensive advice and intelligent logistics ensure that all MULTIVAC solutions are successfully deployed worldwide. Founded in 1961 in a small garage in Böhen and now firmly rooted in the idyllic German region of Allgäu, our group of companies has quickly developed into a global player and a trusted provider of integrated solutions. sales and service companies are part of the MULTIVAC Group.

title: The MULTIVAC Group is investing once again at its site in the Allgäu - Sustainable Packaging News
content: # The MULTIVAC Group is investing once again at its site in the Allgäu. **As part of an official ceremony, the Management Board of the MULTIVAC Group today turned the first spadeful of earth for a new production factory, which is intended for manufacturing parts and handling spare parts logistics in Wolfertschwenden. The new factory with an area of 35,000 square metres is being built about 1,000 metres away from the Group's headquarters, and it is due to be completed by the end of 2025. The new building in direct proximity to our headquarters is a crucial decision for MULTIVAC, and also a clear affirmation once again by our company owners of the Allgäu site. “Thanks to the latest production technology and a high degree of automation, the new factory will significantly expand our output capacity in parts manufacturing and spare parts logistics. At the same time we will also use the new factory, which is due to be gradually brought into operation from 2026, to further optimise the supply of spare parts.
